text: The structures build without std (only alloc) and pull in no uuid or serde_json: std and uuid come with the log and the knowledge model, and serde (with alloc only) with the serde feature.

title: Graph and Tree serialize their content, and read back checked
body: With the serde feature, a Graph writes {nodes: [{key, data}], edges: [{key, from, to, data}]} in key order and a Tree {nodes: [{key, parent, data}]} in preorder (parents first, siblings in order): content only, so equal structures write the same bytes whatever their slots (tests/serde.rs checks it after churn). Reading goes through add_node, add_edge and insert, so a duplicate key, a missing parent or an edge to a missing node fails instead of building a broken structure. Sequences rather than maps, so any key type works in any format. The serde feature no longer turns std on: serde is built with alloc, and std adds serde/std, so a no_std user (parda on wasm) can serialize too; CI builds that for wasm32. The round-trip tests use serde_json, so they live in tests/serde.rs, owned by the crate's root rather than Structures, whose rules keep serde_json out of the structures.
